commitResults.messageBody: Move banner rendering, formatted messages, command input, and scanner lifecycle out of Shan. This gives console I/O one responsibility while preserving existing chatbot behavior and prepares the main class for later Parser, Storage, and TaskList extractions.

Move the data-file path, save/load operations, and saved-task parsing out of Shan. Storage now accepts an OS-independent relative Path and returns an immutable load result containing valid tasks and the skipped-entry count, preserving corruption warnings and rollback behavior while giving persistence one responsibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract user input interpretation into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move command classification, task-number parsing, task argument validation, dated task construction, and date-range parsing out of Shan. Parser remains stateless and returns immutable parsed values or domain tasks, leaving command execution, persistence, and list mutation in Shan while preserving existing responses.

Move mutable list ownership, one-based task access, add/delete/restore operations, and immutable persistence snapshots out of Shan. Preserve command-specific validation messages and failed-save rollback behavior while preparing the chatbot for instance-based composition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Compose Shan as an application instance
commitResults.messageBody: Replace static Ui, Storage, and TaskList state with per-instance collaborators and move startup loading plus command processing into run(). This preserves console and persistence behavior while establishing the dependency boundary needed for command objects to execute against the application services.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command execution into command objects
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce an abstract Command API and concrete add, delete, mark, unmark, list, date-query, and exit commands. Make Parser construct executable commands and reduce Shan's run loop to orchestration while preserving UI formatting, persistence updates, and failed-save rollback behavior.
